text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA

- Main board of Montenegro's ruling Democratic Party of Socialists is convening on Monday, expected to endorse Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's candidacy for president but not proposed changes of the federal constitution.

- The majority of citizens of Vojvodina would vote for the Serbian Radical Party (SRS) and for SRS president Vojislav Seselj as Serbian president if elections were held now according to a poll conducted at the end of May by Scan agency from Novi Sad.
- Serbian medics reached an agreement with government to end their six-week strike and agreed to return to hospitals and clinics on Monday.
- Serb-Kosovo Albanian dialogue continuing in the southern Adriatic city of Ulcinj Monday is expected to gather some 70 intellectuals from Serbia, Macedonia and Montenegro.
- Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) will not take part at the meeting of parliamentary parties convened by Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.
- Coffee price in Serbia grew by 20 percent due to shut down of illegal border crossings. The closure of crossing with eastern Slavonia in Croatia affected the market.
- Serbian agriculture ministry has forbidden export of livestock and only allows exports of meat products.
- Police in Kosovo has arrested 16 Kosovo Albanians in the past ten days accusing them of belonging to an illegal territorial defence, says the Kosovo information centre.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav and Croatian commissions examined in Belgrade regulations on property of refugees and displaced persons, talks to continue in Zagreb in early July.
- British business delegation is visiting Belgrade to examine bilateral economic cooperation.

- Yugoslavia should start implementing the value added tax law as soon as possible because foreigners wish to invest where unified tax regulations are applied, said Yugoslav Foreign Trade Minister Borisav Vukovic.
- Production of health food is Yugoslavia's export opportunity because up to 82 percent of arable land is ecologically pure, said Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic.
- Yugoslav women chess players from chess club Gosa of Smederevska Palanka win at European chess championship in Rijeka, Croatia.
BORBA
- The Soko Stark confectionary factory expects to earn $20 million from exports by end of year.
DANAS
- The opposition coalition Zajedno could not win 50 percent of the votes in Serbia at the moment, said Zoran Djindjic leader of the Democratic Party, one of the coalition partners.

- Mandate of Yugoslavia's president expires on Wednesday, his functions will be carried out by speaker of the lower house of the Yugoslav Parliament Srdja Bozovic for a month, according to the constitution.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- From June 30, all goods from Yugoslavia entering Eastern Slavonia region in Croatia will be subject to Croatian customs regulations, says UNTAES Civilian Affairs chief Gerard Fisher.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Belgian firm Interblue to buy majority stake worth 25 million German marks in Niksic brewery Trebjesa.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA

- There is an absolute political consensus in Montenegro not to allow federal constitutional changes, said Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic. He said Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic or any other candidate for the post of federal president should present his election programme.

- A group of American congressmen wrote to Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic requesting that he reconfirm committments under the Dayton peace accord on human rights and media freedoms. They said Bulatovic's backing of recent political initatives from Belgrade are contrary to his assurances given last year in Washignton.

- The Plevlja coal mine made a profit of 25.3 million dinars in the first three months of 1997. It produced 488,246 tonnes of coal in the first five months of this year, which is seven percent below plan. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
